A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Conformal Prediction for Hierarchical Data. Their main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original Monte Carlo simulations evaluating coverage and prediction-set efficiency on synthetic hierarchical data.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain these original simulation results, including comparisons between plain and reconciled conformal prediction.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–5 retain the same regression, projection, covariance estimation, calibration, and prediction-set construction procedures. Expanded explanations do not introduce a method component or procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six synthetic hierarchy configurations and joint-coverage and component-wise tasks. The image downsampling/upsampling application suggested in v4 Remark 4 is not evaluated.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain plain versus hierarchical ellipsoidal SCP and the component-wise methods Direct, OLS, WLS, Combi, and MinT, including in Appendix F.

E3.justification: Appendix F retains one million observations, the 40%/20%/20%/20% training/estimation/calibration/test split, GAM fitting settings, 90% coverage targets, and the same evaluation metrics and joint-coverage matrix choices.

E4.justification: The hierarchy-size comparisons, MinT instability analysis, and node-level coverage and efficiency analyses in Appendix F.3 remain unchanged. Figures 3–4 retain the same plotted evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 Monte Carlo runs and the same confidence-interval constructions in Appendices F.2.2 and F.3.2. The new discussion of overlapping intervals does not introduce additional runs or a new statistical test.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. Section 5 newly reports the qualitative finding that the best and second-best intervals overlap in every component-wise table row, with no statistically significant differences between them exhibited by the 1,000 runs.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects PH = P to PH = H in the explanation preceding Theorem 2. The theorem already used PH = H in v3, making this a limited mathematical correction. The new global Assumption 1 restates the existing hierarchical-data setting; the substantive theorems and appendix proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: combining conformal prediction with reconciliation and establishing efficiency guarantees for joint and component-wise coverage.

C2.justification: New Remarks 2–3 explicitly explain that already coherent base forecasts receive no efficiency improvement. Section 5 explains the relatively large error bars through the broad family of simulated distributions and adds image processing as a possible future application.

D1.justification: V4 adds an explicit experiment-code availability statement and GitHub link in the abstract; v3 only refers to submitted code. Appendix F's hardware, runtime, data-generation, and implementation information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds Banerjee et al. (2014), Doumèche et al. (2025), and Taieb et al. (2017), clarifying terminology, positioning reconciliation relative to constraint-aware training, and motivating component-wise uncertainty. Several other references receive publication metadata updates while retaining the same cited works.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized expansions to the introduction, notation, assumptions, and experimental discussion, alongside wording corrections, updated affiliations, and acknowledgments. The section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds publication headers, changes float placement and page flow, and expands Figure 1's caption with explicit summation relationships. Existing algorithm boxes, tables, and plots retain their essential visual structure and content.

improvement.justification: V4 improves clarity and reproducibility information through the code link, correction of the misstated projection condition, and clearer qualifications about coherent forecasts and uncertain performance differences. These are useful refinements to an already substantially complete paper; the algorithms, numerical evidence, and main theoretical results remain unchanged.
